summary: Unexpected deduction of reserved credits for KV-cache prefetch/warmup during maintenance window
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed immediate deduction of reserved capacity credits and a matching hosted-usage charge during a scheduled maintenance window. The customer runs periodic KV-cache prefetch/warmup jobs to prime models on dedicated pools. During our regional maintenance the warmup traffic appears to have been routed to hosted fallback shards and also counted against the dedicated reserved-hour bucket, resulting in double-billing and a negative provisional credit balance.

Impact:
- Customer reports ~28,000 token-equivalent deduction from reserved credits and a separate hosted usage line for the same window (~$420).
- Affects production inference for low-latency endpoints using kv-cache warmup scripts (not user-facing inference but counts toward billing).
- Customer is flagged for potential overage and has paused automated jobs until resolved.

Environment:
- Prod / us-east (primary), maintenance event in us-east-1 on 2026-03-12 02:00-03:30 UTC.
- Customer on Dedicated (reserved pool id dp-57a9).
- Endpoints affected: warmup-job route /internal/kv-warmup, pinned to model: redwood/gptx-4-qlora-8k.

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1) Schedule KV-cache warmup job to fan out 3000 requests of 30 tokens each to pinned dedicated model during maintenance window.
2) Platform maintenance triggers fallback routing to hosted pool for a short period.
3) Customer sees immediate reserved-credit deduction and a hosted usage line for the same tokens.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate consumption recorded (reserved + hosted) for the warmup window.
- Billing UI shows reserved credits consumed at 2026-03-12T02:07 and hosted usage posted at 2026-03-12T02:08.
- Provisional invoice shows a negative credit hold and sent autopay alert.

Expected behavior:
- Warmup traffic routed to hosted fallback should be billed only to hosted usage (no reserved-credit deduction), or if reserved pool accepted traffic then fallback should not double-count. Reserved credits should reflect only actual served tokens on the dedicated pool.

Logs / evidence attached by customer:
- Warmup job logs with timestamps and request IDs (prefetch-logs.txt).
- Billing invoice snapshot and provisional line items (invoice-2026-03-12.pdf).
- Warmup request IDs sample: rq_3b7f9c, rq_3b7fdd, rq_3b80a1.

Initial investigation notes:
- Support: verified customer pool dp-57a9 shows an autoscale event and several rejected accept-connection errors coinciding with maintenance.
- Billing: provisional postback shows both a reserved-hour debit (internal tag reserved:dp-57a9) and a hosted postback for the same request ids. Timestamps are within 1 minute of each other.
- Routing: early hypothesis is a race where the routing controller forwarded attempts to the dedicated pool while the fallback proxy also accepted and forwarded the same requests to hosted shards during connection handoff. This could create two meter events: one attributed to reserved and one to hosted.

Immediate customer impact and mitigation taken:
- Support recommended customer pause warmup jobs until fix confirmed. Customer has paused jobs and requested expedited resolution.
- Finance flagged provisional invoice to prevent automated autopay for 48 hours pending reconciliation.

Next steps / action items:
- ENG (serving-runtime & routing) to confirm if there is a known race in routing handoff that emits duplicate metering events when fallback activates. Link to slack thread #incidents-routing-246810.
- Billing to correlate postback IDs and tag sources to produce a provisional credit if double-count confirmed.
- SRE to review autoscaler logs for dp-57a9 and proxy handoff timestamps (window 2026-03-12T02:00-02:10Z).
- Create a short mitigation to dedupe postbacks by request id across reserved/hosted at the reconciler layer if not already present.

Related references:
- Related incident: INC-20260312-01
- Possible linked internal ticket: INT-5102 (routing handoff investigation)
- Customer-facing doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/kv-cache-warmup-billing-notes

Resolution: In Progress (pending ENG confirmation and reconciler credit issuance).
comments: 2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reported duplicate consumption during maintenance. Collected logs and provisional invoice. Escalating to ENG and Billing.
2026-03-12 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Confirmed autoscaler failures for dp-57a9 between 02:03-02:09Z. Proxy handoff logs show simultaneous forward attempts to hosted-shard hst-12.
2026-03-12 - Lina Chen (Billing): Found matching postback IDs that were accepted by both reserved reconciler and hosted reconciler. Marked for provisional credit if engineering confirms duplication.
2026-03-13 - Dev Team (routing): Investigating race where handoff ACK path emits meter event before reserved accept is rolled back; creating dedupe patch proposal. Assigned INT-5102 to routing lead.
2026-03-13 - Support: Notified customer that we are investigating, finance has paused autopay for 48h. Requested sample request ids and warmup schedule for replay.
